columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Created after disrupted communications from the 2011 Tōhoku earthquake; later released publicly and grew through customizable design and stickers.
As of August 2024, ~97M monthly active users in Japan (≈78% of the population); early 2026 reports 100M+ MAUs in Japan, the most widely used platform in the country.
Covers ~78.6% of Japan’s population; widely used across age groups, especially people in their 40s–50s.
Messaging and calling with text, stickers, photos, videos, voice calls, and group chats; social status updates and Instagram-like Stories.

strengths.title: Default communication channel in Japan
strengths.detail: Used for personal and work communication; many people rely on LINE exclusively for social media and messaging.

strengths.title: All-in-one app with payments
strengths.detail: Combines chat, calls, Stories, and LINE Pay, a lighter WeChat-style stack for social and financial interactions.

strengths.title: Strong brand and advertising reach
strengths.detail: With >100M users and high penetration, LINE ads and official accounts can reach large portions of Japan’s population.

strengths.title: Distinct culture and stickers
strengths.detail: Stickers and LINE Friends character branding create a unique, playful UX attractive to Japanese users.

weaknesses.title: Regionally concentrated
weaknesses.detail: Dominant in Japan and some parts of East/Southeast Asia, but far less used globally than WhatsApp or Telegram.

weaknesses.title: Platform dependence for brands
weaknesses.detail: Brands targeting Japanese audiences often need LINE in addition to global stacks, adding complexity.

weaknesses.title: Everything-app UX can feel crowded
weaknesses.detail: Combining chat, Stories, payments, and services in one app can feel overwhelming and harder to design for deep focus.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. LINE is japan’s leading messaging and social app, chat, calls, Stories, stickers, and LINE Pay for 100M+ monthly active users. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

LINE is Japan’s leading messaging and social media app, combining chat, calls, social feeds, stickers, and cashless payments for over 100 million monthly active users. Official site.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and LINE side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On LINE you can use Community & Messaging as a first-class product job. The job is hanging out, announcements, and live conversation, not packaging knowledge into something strangers can browse later.

Using Kahana with LINE

You can use both. LINE keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep live conversation on LINE. Pin a Kahana hub or Club link in a channel, discuss live there, and assign the next ebook, video, or course from Kahana so the syllabus is not buried in the thread.
